plain: To grow weaker or smaller over time

webster.text: To be diminished; to decrease; particularly applied to the illuminated part of the moon.

more.text: To decline; to fail; to sink; as the waning age of life.

example.quote: It is already on the wane, eclipsed by the enlarging orb of reason, and the luminous revolutions of America and France.
example.cite: Thomas Paine, Rights of Man, Parts One and Two (London, 1791-92)
